catalog_quote: p.152: "Different from the other Northern Songhay languages and Tuareg, Tasawaq is a tone language. From the old Songhay system (Nicolai 1981: 207ff.), it preserves three tones, Low, High, and Falling. The Falling tone has only restricted oppositional value, as it can only occur in CVV syllables and in CVC syllables with a final sonorant. In most cases it goes back to an initial Low tone in an all-Low contour. In all-Low contours with an initial syllable of another type, the initial Low tone is realised as a High tone." ... p.153: "Tasawaq verbs of Songhay origin with one or two syllables show all combinations of High and Low tones which are logically possible." ... p.157: "In addition to the difference in vowel length and quality, there is also an accentual difference between Short Perfective and Long Perfective in Tuareg (for a description of the intricate accent system of Tuareg, see…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tasawaq is described as a lexical/grammatical tone language (H, L, restricted Falling; downdrift, polar and floating tones per Kossmann 2015:84-86). No word stress or accent is posited; the only mention of accent is that Tuareg lexical accent is converted into H tone when words are borrowed, i.e. prominence is encoded tonally. No source opened states a stress position.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal particulars: Falling tone confined to CVV and sonorant-closed CVC; underlying all-Low words surface with initial Falling/High in isolation (Kossmann 2015:84, contra Nicolaï 1980:248-250).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone; Kossmann 2015 also describes phrase-level downdrift and sandhi (polar tone on clitics). Data from one speaker (Mrs. Ibrahim, In-Gall origin, resident in Agadez) whose variety differs somewhat (pharyngealized consonants) from Nicolaï's and Alidou's consultants.
new_statements.identity_note: All Kossmann data (2007, 2012, 2015) come from a single speaker, Mrs. Ibrahim (née Nana Mariama Aweïssou), a native of In-Gall living in Agadez, whose idiolect has pharyngealized consonants absent from Nicolaï's and Alidou's In-Gall consultants; Kossmann treats this as dialect-internal variation within Tasawaq (tasa1240, 'ingelsi' in Nicolaï's terminology). No separate glottocode involved.

sources.note: Sec. 2, pp. 84-86: tone system of the speaker's variety - two level tones H and L plus Falling (restricted to long vowels / sonorant-closed syllables), downdrift, no all-Low polysyllables in isolation, polar tone on clitics, floating tones. Nothing on stress/accent.
